title: An investigation of young adults' psychophysiological and self-report responses to paid partnership disclosures in pro-oral nicotine pouch videos.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION
Oral nicotine pouches (ONPs) have surged in popularity on social media, in part due to promotions by influencers. This study examined how the presence or absence of a "paid partnership" disclosure in an influencer, ONP TikTok video impacted psychophysiological and self-report responses of young adults who use ONPs.

STUDY DESIGN
Using a between-participant design, participants viewed one of two, 2-minute TikTok simulations that either did or did not have a paid partnership disclosure in an influencer video promoting ONPs during the Fall of 2024.

SETTING/PARTICIPANTS
The study was conducted in a media psychophysiology research laboratory and included 96 young-adults (ages 18-23) who had used ONPs within the past 30 days.

INTERVENTION
Participants' heart rates were measured during the TikTok simulation, and they answered self-report questions about ONPs before and after viewing the simulation.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
Primary outcomes included self-reported craving, perceived harm reduction, behavioral intentions, and heart rate as a psychophysiological indicator of cognitive resource allocation.

RESULTS
Data were analyzed in the Spring of 2025. Psychophysiological data indicated greater cognitive resource allocation among participants who viewed the video with the paid partnership disclosure compared to those who viewed the video without the disclosure (p=.03). Self-report measures revealed significant increases from baseline between message conditions, with craving, perceived harm reduction, and behavioral intentions to use ONPs increasing more among participants who viewed the video with the disclosure than among those who viewed the video without the disclosure (all p-values<.001).

CONCLUSIONS
Paid partnership disclosures in an influencer-generated message promoting ONPs facilitate attention to the message, heighten craving and intentions to use, and reduce perceived harm of ONPs. These findings can be applied in counter-messaging efforts including testing if leveraging influencers to create user-generated content with paid partnership disclosures can effectively inform young-adults about the potential risks of ONP use.
